What is the essential teaching in 'The Language of the Heart'?

In 'The Language of the Heart', the teaching opens with this observation: *"The Venerable Ācariya Mun taught that all hearts have the same language."* The central invitation is to turn one's investigation inward — to verify the Dhamma not as a set of beliefs, but as directly observable reality in one's own body, speech, and mind. As the text teaches, the Dhamma is *akāliko* — ever-present — and *opanayiko* — leading inward — available to be known (*paccattaṁ*) by each practitioner for themselves. There is no need to search elsewhere; the truth is already here.
